text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash involve the scalp, eyebrows, or behind the ears, and is it associated with any crusting or oozing? Have you noticed any similar rashes in skin folds like the armpits or groin, or any signs of eczema elsewhere on his body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: This presentation of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead, exacerbated by cold weather, is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, also known as cradle cap in infants. Do the scales lift easily without bleeding, and is the baby otherwise feeding and sleeping well?
